result.summary:
Independent re-verification of WF02-REQ-036 at commit 95ce0c5 on feature/WF02-REQ-036, per GitHub issue #68 / docs/agents/requirements.yaml REQ-036, against docs/agents/design/REQ-036.md and the actual current code (not the handoff trail's narration). All checks re-run from scratch in this session; none copied from prior reports.

Re-run checks (all foreground, blocking): `npm run lint -w apps/bot` -- clean, zero errors/warnings. `npm run build -w apps/bot` (tsc) -- clean, zero type errors. `npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism` from repo root, run twice per ISS-0031 protocol: run 1 = 41/41 files, 367/367 tests, 47.75s; run 2 = 41/41 files, 367/367 tests, 42.57s. Identical results both times, no varying failing-file set, no FK-violation contention symptom observed -- ISS-0031's pattern did not reproduce.

Independent AC-by-AC re-verification against actual code/tests (not the trail's summary):
- AC1: read urgencyJobs.db.test.ts in full. Event exactly 48h from starts_at with 2 requested registrations -> both pushed to the chapter's one organizer (getPrimaryOrganizerIdForChapter) and both ledgered under 'pending_request_urgent'; a sibling event 49h out in the SAME test run surfaces zero sends/ledger rows for its own registration; the list marker (isRequestUrgent via listPendingRequestsForOrganizer) independently verified true/false for the two events. Matches design §2.1/§2.2/§2.4/§2.5. PASS.
- AC2: read the AC2 block in autoDeclineJobs.db.test.ts. 3 pending + 1 pre-admitted + 1 pre-rejected -> exactly 3 transitions to 'rejected', exactly 3 sends/ledger rows, admitted/rejected rows and their audit trails untouched, audit count asserted before/after (+3 exactly). PASS.
- AC3: read the captured message assertions directly -- text contains 'was not decided before registration closed' and 'Nobody reviewed and declined it', explicitly asserts the ABSENCE of merit-based phrasing ('not good enough', 'not qualified', 'your application', 'you were not accepted'), and contains the exact reused deepLinkSeeUpcoming onward-path string. PASS, and independently spot-checked per this role's mandatory-minimum instruction.
- AC4 (mandatory spot-check): read domain/registration.ts's autoDeclineRequest (lines ~1960-2006) and decideRejectionOutcome (~1859-1868) directly, and the AC4 test block (autoDeclineJobs.db.test.ts lines 272-329). Confirmed the two-mechanism trace holds in the actual code: Mechanism 2 is decideRejectionOutcome's `admission !== 'requested'` branch inside autoDeclineRequest's own SELECT...FOR UPDATE + transaction (state guard, zero dependency on notification_ledger); Mechanism 1 is sendLedgeredNotification's own UNIQUE(registration_id, kind) INSERT (send guard, zero dependency on registrations.admission). The test calls job.run() twice at the same evaluationTime with 3 seeded pending requests: run 1 = 3 sends/3 transitions/audit count baseline+3; run 2 = still 3 sends total (0 new), still 3 'rejected' rows (0 further transitions), audit count unchanged, ledger rows still exactly 1 each (not 2). Note: the test simulates 'restart, run again' by calling job.run() a second time in-process rather than literally killing the OS process -- this is a faithful equivalent because (a) I independently confirmed by reading both scheduler files that neither carries any in-memory state across .run() invocations -- every candidate list and every state check is re-queried fresh from the DB inside .run(), exactly what a restarted process's own first tick would do -- and (b) the test's full-batch-then-full-batch-again shape is a strictly stronger exercise of the state/ledger guards than the narrower single-candidate mid-batch kill, since it re-validates the guard against ALL three rows already being in their post-transition state, not just some. This matches the design's own §4 trace precisely. PASS.
- AC5 (mandatory spot-check): read domain code's absence of any registrationClosesAt read inside autoDeclineRequest (confirmed -- it only takes registrationId/at, the NULL-vs-endsAt branching lives entirely in the CALLER'S selection query, scheduler/autoDeclineJobs.ts's selectRegistrationsForAutoDecline, read directly: `(registrationClosesAt IS NOT NULL AND registrationClosesAt <= evaluationTime) OR (registrationClosesAt IS NULL AND endsAt <= evaluationTime)`). Verified both directions in the test file: (a) NULL registrationClosesAt, evaluationTime just AFTER endsAt -> auto-declines exactly as a non-null close would (1 send, row->'rejected', 1 audit row with actorUserId NULL, registrationClosesAt still NULL afterward -- no column added); (b) the SAME NULL event evaluated BEFORE endsAt -> zero sends, row remains 'requested'. Both directions genuinely exercised, not merely asserted. PASS.
- AC6: exactly one audit_log row per auto-decline, actorUserId NULL, asserted per-row inside the AC2 test block and again standalone in the AC5-NULL test; counted before/after in the AC2/AC4 blocks. PASS.
- AC7: both urgency-side and auto-decline-side broadcast_opt_in=false/blocked=true cases read directly in both test files -- broadcastOptIn=false recipients receive exactly one message, blocked=true recipients receive zero and get no ledger row (blocked check precedes the ledger insert, matching sendLedgeredNotification's existing unconditional order), and for the auto-decline side the blocked registrant's row still transitions to 'rejected' with its own audit row (state and notification are correctly independent). PASS.
- AC8: grepped and read urgencyJobs.ts and autoDeclineJobs.ts directly -- zero inline literal user-facing English text in either file; both route every composed string through getCatalog(lang)/catalog.autoDecline.notification. The AC8 test asserts both the positive (catalog call present) and negative (provisional English sentence text NOT hardcoded in the job file) conditions programmatically. The catalog key-set parity check (i18n/catalogs.test.ts) is part of the full suite that passed both runs. Confirmed en.ts/ru.ts both carry urgentMarker/urgentNotification/autoDecline.notification with matching key shapes in types.ts. The provisional-wording disclosure is recorded verbatim in handoffs/WF02-REQ-036/step-02-backend-dev.json result.issues[0] (exact EN strings quoted) -- present and correctly framed as pending product-owner review, matching REQ-014/REQ-032 precedent. PASS.

Scope discipline, independently confirmed: `git diff master...feature/WF02-REQ-036 -- apps/bot/src/domain/registration.ts` shows zero removed/modified lines (grep for '^-' matches only the diff header) -- the entire diff to this file is additive (getPrimaryOrganizerIdForChapter, autoDeclineRequest, both new). rejectRequest (REQ-035) is byte-for-byte unchanged: same signature (db, registrationId, organizerUserId, reason, at), same non-nullable organizerUserId, same 'registration.reject' audit action, same reason-in-payload shape. `git diff master...feature/WF02-REQ-036 --stat -- apps/bot/src/db/ apps/bot/drizzle` returns empty -- no schema or migration changes anywhere in this branch, confirming the design's own 'no DATA-DESIGNER needed' claim independently rather than trusting it. Full branch diff stat shows only the 13 files the design document names, all under apps/bot/**, zero apps/web/** changes.

No discrepancy found between any prior report and the actual code/tests. TEST-RUNNER's 367/367-twice claim reproduced exactly. REVIEWER/SECURITY-REVIEWER/TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR PASS gates are independently corroborated by direct inspection of the code and tests they gated, not merely re-read as narration.

acceptance_criteria_verdict.AC1: PASS -- re-read test + independently confirmed selection/push/marker code paths
acceptance_criteria_verdict.AC2: PASS -- re-read test, exact transition/send/audit counts confirmed
acceptance_criteria_verdict.AC3: PASS -- re-read captured message assertions directly
acceptance_criteria_verdict.AC4: PASS (mandatory spot-check) -- re-read autoDeclineRequest/decideRejectionOutcome source and the double-run test; confirmed no in-memory state crosses .run() calls, making the in-process double-run a faithful restart-safety equivalent
acceptance_criteria_verdict.AC5: PASS (mandatory spot-check) -- re-read selectRegistrationsForAutoDecline's NULL-fallback SQL and both directions of the NULL-registrationClosesAt test
acceptance_criteria_verdict.AC6: PASS -- audit row count and actorUserId NULL confirmed in three separate test blocks
acceptance_criteria_verdict.AC7: PASS -- broadcast_opt_in/blocked behavior confirmed for both urgency and auto-decline sends
acceptance_criteria_verdict.AC8: PASS -- catalog-only string sourcing confirmed by direct file read plus programmatic negative-literal assertion; provisional-wording disclosure confirmed present in step-02 handoff
